_comment: Stock-adjustment approval-gate golden fixtures (issue #50, extended #170, #189). Run against the Dart DAO (requestStockAdjustment/approveRequest/rejectRequest) AND the SQL RPCs request_stock_adjustment/approve_stock_adjustment (0141). Rule: pending => no inventory change; approve => apply delta; reject => no change. status+inventory pinned on both arms. 'request' scenarios pin the stock-keeper->pending path on the Dart arm; the RPC arm skips them (its Tier-2 identity is the CEO, whom the server routes to immediate-apply). #170 #7a adds COST semantics on the Dart DAO: an approved increase creates a Cost Batch, an approved decrease draws the FIFO queue down and snapshots the drawn value onto the adjustment (dart_snapshot_value_kobo / dart_new_batch_cost_kobo). #189: the approval carries no cost of its own, so the increase's batch takes the product's RECORDED cost (product_buying_price_kobo, a Dart-arm-only seed) and is Uncosted (0) only when the product has no cost on file — batching at 0 with a price on file made those units sell at 0 COGS forever (#41's backfill fires only on a 0->positive cost edit). Those scenarios are dart_arm_only — the web RPC cost pass is out of scope (flagged to the web repo), so the RPC arm skips them, same precedent as the #175 money-track scenarios. inflow_cost_kobo seeds a costed batch of start_qty before the op.

scenarios.name: stock keeper request creates a pending row, no inventory change
approving an add applies the delta
approving a remove applies the negative delta
rejecting a request makes no inventory change
#189: approving an increase batches it at the product's recorded cost
#7a: approving an increase of a product with NO cost on file creates an Uncosted (0) batch
#7a: approving a remove draws the FIFO queue down and snapshots the drawn value
